newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan tells Major of Indian missile threat.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan tells Major of Indian missile threat.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari told British Prime Minister John Major on Monday that India's missile programme was a danger to Islamabad and the whole South Asian region, the official APP news agency said.
In the talks between the two leaders on the second day of Major's three-day visit to Pakistan, Leghari spoke of the "damage that Indian policies were causing to the entire region", it said.

APP quoted the president as telling Major that India's deployment of the short-range surface-to-surface "Prithvi missile and continued development of long-range missiles... poses a threat to the entire region".
"The latest Indian missiles have reduced the reaction time for Pakistan and have thereby multiplied the threat to it," Leghari said.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over the disputed Himalayan region of Kashmir.

APP quoted Major as telling Leghari that a settlement of the Kashmir dispute would "unleash the potential for development of the region" and that Britain would be happy to play its part to help find a solution.
"Political will and courage could be called for in both Pakistan and India to settle the problem of Kashmir," Major was quorted as saying.
India is fighting a separatist revolt in two-thirds of Kashmir it rules and accuses Islamabad of training and arming Kashmiri militants fighting for independence or union with Pakistan.
Pakistan, which controls the remaining third of the region, denies the charge and says its support for them is only moral and political.
